$doc: Link grid's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component link-grid` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/link-grid.tsx. Same contract as components/button/definition.json: a plain string is a structural literal, {"token": "x"} binds --x, and an array is a sequence of both. LINK-GRID IS THE BLOCK THAT FORCED A SCOPED PART. Its cells are bare <a> elements with no class of their own, so there is nothing for a `selector` to name; the part NAMES the rule it lives `within` and gives the `element` path under it, and the emitter supplies the combinator. That is the whole of the relation this schema admits — a descendant of the root, and nothing else. The two border declarations are the block's one real idea: the grid draws its top and left edges once, and every cell draws its own right and bottom, so a wrapped row of cells has no doubled rule anywhere and no cell knows how many siblings it has.

rules.name: cell
rules.$doc: One channel. `flex: 1 1 11rem` is the whole responsive behaviour — cells share the row until one would be narrower than 11rem, and then the row wraps; there is no breakpoint here and there is nothing for one to do. Its border is the mirror of the root's: right and bottom, so the two together draw a closed grid whatever the wrap lands on.

rules.name: hover
rules.$doc: The cell inverts to ink rather than tinting, because every cell is equal weight and a tint would read as one of them being the primary action. The primary contact action is the display link elsewhere on the page.
